title: The dashboard
summary: What the home screen shows, who sees what, and how to rearrange it.
html:
The dashboard is the first screen after logging in, and it shows a different thing to each kind of person. A staff member sees the work waiting for them. A customer contact logging into the portal sees their own quotes, invoices and tickets and nothing else.

What is on it

The dashboard is assembled from widgets, each supplied by a plugin. The ones most installations see are:

  • Alerts — overdue invoices, quotes awaiting approval, tasks due. This is the part worth reading every morning.
  • Summary figures — amounts invoiced, amounts paid, hours logged, grouped by period.
  • Recent activity — the records touched most recently.

If a widget is missing, the plugin that provides it is probably switched off. Check Settings → Plugins before looking for a dashboard setting.

Rearranging it

Widget layout is saved per person, not per installation, so moving a widget changes only your own dashboard. Drag a widget by its heading to move it. The layout is stored against your user account and the screen you were on, so it survives logging out.

When the numbers look wrong

The summary figures are calculated from the records as they stand, not from a stored total, so they cannot drift out of step. If a figure looks wrong, the usual causes are:

  • A date range that is not the one you assumed. Most summaries default to the current financial year, which is set in Configuration.
  • Invoices that are entered but not marked as paid. An invoice counts as income when a payment is recorded against it, not when it is sent.
  • A second currency. Totals are shown in the system currency; see Currencies.
